newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RAMSEY TO COME OUT OF RETIREMENT FOR RED WINGS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RAMSEY TO COME OUT OF RETIREMENT FOR RED WINGS.

text.p: Seventeen-year NHL defenceman Mike Ramsey has decided to come out of retirement and will return to play for the Detroit Red Wings, the club said on Thursday.

Ramsey, 36, appeared in just 80 games from 1994-96 for Detroit before retiring after last year's playoffs. He had two goals and four assists with a plus-18 rating in 47 contests last season, and added four assists in 15 playoff games.
"We've been speaking to Mike for the past few weeks," said Detroit head coach Scotty Bowman. "He has been following our season very closely and is excited about returning to our organisation.
"Mike has remained in excellent shape and will arrive on Tuesday to work closely with our trainer John Wharton in hope of returning to our lineup in two weeks."

After being selected with the 11th overall pick by Buffalo in the 1979 NHL Draft and helping Team USA to the "Miracle on Ice" at the 1980 Winter Olympics, Ramsey joined the Sabres late in the 1979-80 campaign.
He played 12 full seasons with Buffalo and parts of two others before being dealt to Pittsburgh in March 1993. The four-time All-Star collected 79 goals and 266 assists in 1,068 career NHL games.
Detroit is currently 28-19-11 and stands five points behind Dallas for first place in the Central Division.
